primary.question: Can a viva be waived for a professional doctorate, and who decides?
primary.expected_answer: Permission to waive a viva on first submission will only be granted by the Dean in exceptional circumstances. The Postgraduate Research Education Team would then notify the student of the examiners' wish not to hold a viva and the reasons for it, and the student would be told they have the right to have a viva if they wish.
primary.actual_answer:
Yes, a viva can be waived for a professional doctorate, but only in specific circumstances, and the decision rests with the **Dean**.

According to both the general Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates (2025-26) and the Code of Practice: Professional Doctorates Tavistock (2025-26):

- **First submission**: Permission to waive a viva will only be granted by the Dean in exceptional circumstances. The Postgraduate Research Education Team notifies the student of the examiners' wish not to hold a viva and the reasons, but the student retains the right to have a viva if they wish.
- **Referred thesis**: If the recommended outcome is a pass, a request to waive the viva will normally be granted. If the recommendation is not a pass, waiving the viva will only be granted in exceptional circumstances. Again, the student is informed and retains the right to request a viva.

For comparison, the more general Code of Practice on Vivas (2025-26) states that the **Faculty Dean (Postgraduate)** must approve any request to waive a viva, and this is normally only permitted where the viva is for re-examination following referral and examiners agree the candidate can now pass, or where exceptional circumstances prevent the candidate from engaging in the process. Vivas will not be waived if an examiner believes the candidate is likely to fail, only eligible for a lower award, or likely to be referred.

- https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/about/governance/code-practice-vivas.pdf

primary.question: A student has failed a core taught module with a mark of 45. Can that failure be condoned?
primary.expected_answer: No. Condonement applies only to non-core modules - failure with a mark of 40 or more may be condoned for up to 20 credits in non-core modules. All taught core modules must be passed, so a failed core module cannot be condoned regardless of the mark.
primary.actual_answer:
No. Across the postgraduate rules provided, condonement only applies to **non-core** taught modules, not core modules. For example:

- The Postgraduate Diploma rules state a student must "Pass all the taught core modules" as a requirement for the award, with condonement only permitted for "failure with a mark of 40 or more for up to 30 credits in non-core taught modules" ([pg-dip-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/other-pgt-awards/pg-dip-25.pdf)).
- The CSEE accredited Masters variations similarly require passing "all the taught core modules and the dissertation or equivalent," with condonement limited to "non-core taught modules" ([csee-ft-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/csee-ft-masters-accredited-variations-25.pdf)).
- The Health and Social Care modular rules explicitly state: "A core module must be taken as part of the programme structure and passed, with no condonement of marks below a pass allowed" ([modular_25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/department-specific/modular_25.pdf)).
- The Kaplan (KOL) Postgraduate Diploma and Postgraduate Certificate rules also require passing "all the taught core modules," permitting condonement only for non-core modules ([kol-pgdip-roa-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/partner-institutions/kol-pgdip-roa-25.pdf), [kol-pgcert-roa-25.pdf](https://www.essex.ac.uk/-/media/documents/directories/academic-section/rules-of-assessment/pgt/2025-26/partner-institutions/kol-pgcert-roa-25.pdf)).

So a core module mark of 45 (a fail, since the pass mark is 50) cannot be condoned under any of these rules — the student must pass core modules outright, typically through reassessment.
